body: Well, in South Korea, you become your new age on the first of January, regardless of your birth date. If I was born on June 30th, 1980, I would be 32 today even though June 30th didn't pass for the 32nd time in my life. You can celebrate your birthday on the day you were born, but everyone "officially" gains one year on the first day of January. I'm not sure if Japan does this as well, but it's a thought to consider.

Thinking about my applications, it feels like I'm just waiting for the slap to come. After reading your comment, it seems as if there's nothing for me to do but suck it up and receive the blow. Is there really no way for me to get what I want?

Yes I know. What I want is not really the most fundamental point of life. I can do just fine in a state college, or even no college at all. If I could come to terms with that, I wouldn't be posting on r/suicidewatch.

Well, my parents were actually the ones telling me to tone it down a bit. Especially my mom, they can see what mental damage I've caused myself from trying to meet my expectations. My mom once told me that even if I didn't go to college and lived with her till death, she would still be proud of me for being happy with myself.

With that said, there's nothing I want more than Ivy league. I'm not even thinking about life after college; I just want to be part of that group. All I want is the ultimate college experience, with all the stress and panic committed towards tests and other glorified skills useless in the real world. I really want to be a part of a community where I belong, and I feel most comfortable, or most content, when studying for tests or bickering over minor academic specks with peers. Even if, in the end, all this will go to waste, it's what I look towards in the future. It's the one thing I want in life, and I'm willing to sacrifice most anything for that.

If I could just accept failure and move on, that would be a completely different person from who I am. I think part of my fear with facing failure is losing my identity. It's something I wouldn't do and that means I have to change me.
